 Sabres vs. Blue Jackets | How to watch, lineup notes, and storylines
 The Sabres host Hockey Fights Cancer Night and make some key lineup changes.
 By 
 Jourdon LaBarber 
 @jourdonlabarber 
 Sabres.com 
 November 06, 2026 
 Link copied 
 The Buffalo Sabres host the Columbus Blue Jackets at KeyBank Center on Friday in what will be a rematch of opening night for both clubs.
 The Blue Jackets came away from that first meeting in Columbus with a 6-3 win, led by a three-point performance from newly acquired forward Matthew Knies. The Sabres have steadily improved since then, having won three straight games prior to a setback at home against Ottawa on Wednesday.
 Wednesday's Postgame Report: Late mistakes cost Sabres 
 Columbus, meanwhile, has climbed back to .500 with a pair of wins over Western Conference contenders. The Blue Jackets beat the Avalanche 7-2 on Tuesday, then pulled out a 2-1 shootout over the Stars on Thursday.
 Tonight will be the Sabres’ annual Hockey Fights Cancer Night, presented by Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center. Learn more here . 
 How to watch 
 TV (Sabres broadcast market): MSG (Pregame coverage begins at 6:30 p.m.)
 Streaming (Sabres broadcast market):  DAZN
 Radio:  WGR 550 /  Buffalo Sabres App 
 More ways to watch/listen to Sabres games 
 Lineup notes (updated 6:35 p.m.) 
 Jiri Kulich, who missed the last five games after taking a puck to the face in practice and going through concussion protocol, re-enters the lineup in place of Ryan McLeod.
 “Obviously, it’s frustrating being out of the lineup. You want to be out there with your team helping out," McLeod said of the healthy scratch. "Just kind of getting back to basics. I think they could tell I was struggling, and it’s gonna be a fresh start here, hopefully, coming back from sitting one.”
 "It's not about not playing tonight; it's really about what the next game is going to look like," added coach Lindy Ruff, who met with McLeod to discuss his recent performance.
 Conor Timmins will make his season debut on defense, subbing in for Louis Crevier on the third pair. And Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen starts in net.
 Numbers to know 
 Zach Benson enters Friday on a five-game point streak, having scored two goals and six assists in that span.
 Benson’s 12 assists this season lead the Sabres.
 Tage Thompson is one goal shy of tying Miroslav Satan for eighth place on the Sabres’ all-time list (224).
 Thompson’s 11 career goals against Columbus are the most by any Sabres player all-time.
 Peyton Krebs’ goal against Ottawa on Wednesday was his eighth point of the season, his highest total through 15 games of a season in his career.
 Scouting the Blue Jackets 
 The Blue Jackets have allowed a combined three goals in their last two wins over Colorado and Dallas. They allowed two high-danger scoring chances in those games, according to Stathletes – particularly impressive against high-powered offenses featuring the likes of Nathan MacKinnon, Jason Robertson and Mikko Rantanen.
 Zach Werenski, the reigning Norris Trophy winner, scored his first goal of the season in the Dallas win. Kent Johnson made a slick feed on the play for his team-leading 17th point, then scored the winner in the shootout.
 Cam Talbot started on Thursday, so look for Jet Greaves to get the nod in goal against the Sabres. Greaves made 23 saves to earn the win in the opening-night matchup between these two teams.
